Subject: TTFT & streaming constraints — pilot actions and probe plan

Hi Alex / Maria,

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on user flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a short pilot:   

Summary of what you asked for on the call:
- TTFT targets: median <= 120 ms for short responses (~<64 tokens); p95 <= 220 ms for typical prompts (30–100 tokens).
- Concurrency & throughput: steady state ~100 concurrent streams, expected baseline RPS ~120, peak bursts up to ~400 RPS.
- Streaming mode: you prefer server-sent events (SSE) for browser clients but are open to WebSocket for long-lived sessions.
- Chunking cadence: want small frequent chunks — target 60–100 ms cadence or ~24–40 token chunks depending on reply density.

Asks from our side to finalize pilot sizing: 
1) Can you send 2–3 representative prompt+context examples (short/median/long) and an expected response distribution? We attached a sample prompts file to illustrate the format.
2) Confirm expected average token output length and percent of responses that are >128 tokens.
3) Any PII/sensitive content notes (for routing to Private deployment) or is Hosted API acceptable for an initial trial?

Proposed pilot plan (high level):
- Redwood to run a 2-week pilot with streaming telemetry capture + TTFT probes.
- Initial config: SSE with 60–80 ms target chunk cadence; warmstart enabled for heavy endpoints; KV prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Infra: start on shared hosted nodes with 2 dedicated GPUs reserved for pilot (scale if we see higher p95).
- Success criteria: median TTFT <=120ms and p95 <=220ms for a representative workload; no functional regressions on output quality.

Next steps / owners: 
- Alex/Maria: share sample payloads and peak hour schedule (action: Alex) — due: 2026-07-02
- Karthik: scope pilot config and estimate reserved capacity/costs (action: Karthik) — due: 2026-07-06
- Ben: send a short streaming ops note with recommended cadence/priming and fallback behavior (action: Ben) — due: 2026-07-01
- Jordan: prepare pilot runbook & HubSpot update (action: Jordan) — sending runbook draft after Karthik/Ben inputs.

Attachments: clearwave_sample_prompts.json (attached), pilot_runbook_v1.pdf (will attach after internal scoping).

If this matches what you remember, I can schedule a 30-min sync next week to lock dates.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Concurrency: I previously estimated 100 concurrent streams but during peak promos we can get up to ~150 concurrent sessions for ~10–15 minutes. Planning for 150 as a realistic peak is safer.
- Prompt sizes: most requests are 30–70 tokens; ~10% exceed 150 tokens. Typical replies are 40–120 tokens.
- Mode: SSE is preferred for web clients; we have a mobile app that may benefit from WebSocket for long-lived flows — we can flip modes per route.
- Security: we prefer Hosted for quick iteration but will likely need Private (VPC) for PCI-adjacent flows down the road.

Cost sensitivity: we care about per-token costs during the pilot — if you can provide a rough capacity / cost estimate for 2 reserved GPUs vs. burstable hosted, that helps our procurement conversation.

I'll attach an anonymized sample payload set by EOD tomorrow. Happy to do a 30-min sync after you propose slot.

—Alex

Quick technical recommendations based on Alex's profile and target SLAs:

1) Streaming mode: default to SSE for the pilot on web routes. Use WebSocket only for mobile long-lived sessions where reconnection cost is high. Redwood supports both and can route per-route.

2) Chunk cadence: target 70–90 ms cadence for initial pilot. This hits a good balance: small latency per chunk while avoiding exponential overhead on server-side scheduling. Chunk sizing: ~24–40 tokens per chunk; auto-adjust if generator is producing long tokens (e.g., code).

3) Warmstart / priming: use a 3–5 second warmstart (prefix pad) on heavy endpoints during peak windows to reduce cold-start p95. Combine with KV prefix cache for repeated prompts.

4) Fallbacks & graceful degradation:
- If backend p95 breaches 300 ms, fall back to batched non-streaming path (best-effort) for degraded quality but preserving availability.
- Telemetry: capture TTFT, first-chunk-size, chunk-count, reconnects, and per-request token cost. Provide dashboards per-route.

5) Pilot infra: 2 reserved GPUs (A100-class) as Jordan suggested seems fine for initial sizing given 150 peak concurrency. We'll size headroom to ~1.5x expected load. If procurement is sensitive, start hosted burstable with autoscale and set an SLA escalation policy.

I'll convert this into a 1-pager runbook and attach it (ttft_probe_instructions.pdf / pilot_runbook_v1.pdf).
